prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” attorney for every car-accident case — the right lawyer depends on your crash’s facts, injuries, insurance issues, budget, and whether you want someone who will try the case or focus on settlement. I can help you find the best fit, but first I’ll give quick guidance and a few reputable Chicago firms to consider.

Quick next-step question
- What ZIP code or neighborhood are you in, and were there serious injuries or just property damage? (That helps me give a more targeted list.)

What to look for in a car-accident PI attorney
- Experience with car-accident claims and similar injuries (neck/back, fractures, catastrophic, wrongful death)
- Trial experience (if you may need to sue and go to court)
- Track record of settlements/verdicts and client references
- Clear contingency-fee agreement (typical range 33%–40%; costs advanced by firm)
- Who will actually handle your case (attorney vs. paralegal)
- Responsiveness and communication style
- No disciplinary history (check Illinois ARDC)

Reputable Chicago firms you can start with
- Clifford Law Offices — long-established Chicago plaintiff firm handling serious auto accidents and wrongful death
- Romanucci & Blandin — Chicago-based firm known for catastrophic injury and auto-collision cases
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard — prominent in personal injury and wrongful death cases

(If you want, I can compile a longer list tailored to your ZIP code and case details.)

How to vet attorneys quickly
- Read recent client reviews on Google/Yelp, and professional listings on Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo
- Check Illinois Attorney Registration & Disciplinary Commission (ARDC) for discipline history
- Interview 2–3 lawyers (most offer free consultations)

Important questions to ask in a consultation
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled? What were the typical outcomes?
- Have you tried similar cases in Cook County court? What’s your trial record?
- Who will handle day-to-day work on my file?
- How do you charge (contingency %, costs, liens)?
- What do you estimate my case is worth, and why?
- How long will it likely take?

Documents to bring to a first consult
- Police report, photos of crash/damage/injuries
- Medical records and bills, and list of treating providers
- Insurance information (your policy and other driver’s)
- Names/contacts for witnesses
- Repair estimates or receipts

Timing note
- Illinois personal-injury claims generally have a 2-year statute of limitations from the date of the crash (there are exceptions), so it’s best to contact a lawyer soon.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and a brief summary of the crash/injuries and I’ll find 4–6 well-rated Chicago attorneys (with contact details, estimated fees, and recent results) for you to contact.
